order: Master Blueprint Section 14.3 Part B (FBL-100) — persisted browser/DOM owner journey
how_it_was_driven: The REAL console, served by the REAL application, against a REAL database, behind a REAL cookie login. The browser walked `GET /auth/login` and `GET /auth/callback` itself and received its session cookie from the production callback route; nothing fabricated a session row. Only the identity PROVIDER is replaced, at the seam the shipped code already exposes (`useIdentityProviderForTests`): there is no WorkOS to call, and the fake signs genuine tokens with the local issuer so the production verification path — nonce binding included — runs unchanged. Every step below was performed by clicking the console's OWN buttons and filling its OWN form controls, so the handlers that ran are the ones that ship, and each stage records the DOM that resulted. The in-app browser pane does not composite in this environment, so the clicks were dispatched programmatically onto the real DOM elements and the rendered DOM was read back; what is NOT proved here is the pixel-level pointer path, and that is stated rather than glossed.
operator: one person holding sales_manager, salesperson, bdc_agent and inventory_manager — the owner of a small store, who runs the floor and works customers on it
what_the_world_held_before_the_walk: One rooftop (Downtown), one car acquired through Release Train 2's own service (stock A1234), one lead captured, qualified and handed to sales through Release Train 3's, and the operator on the floor rotation. Every row was made by the service that owns it; nothing was planted.

what_this_does_and_does_not_show: SHOWS: the whole FBL-100 operator journey is reachable in a browser, through the shipped console, against real data — arrival, greeting from the up-list, receiving the handoff, shortlisting real stock, a licence-gated test drive and its return, selecting the car, a negotiation round, the stage machine, the manager's board and closing the visit.
SHOWS: two refusals a person actually meets, rendered as readable messages with a correlation id rather than as a stack trace — the unchecked licence and the turnover to oneself.
SHOWS: there is no money on any of these screens, and the one place the subject comes up says the figure does not exist yet and names the release that will bring it.
DOES NOT SHOW: the pixel-level pointer path. The browser pane does not composite in this environment, so clicks were dispatched onto the real elements rather than delivered by a moving cursor.

DOES NOT SHOW: a successful manager turnover or a reassignment, because this one-person store has nobody else to name. Both are covered by tests/sales-journey.test.ts and tests/sales-authority.test.ts.
